_comment: Unseen query wordings for the language-generalisation test. Training only ever uses the 14 canonical sentences in data_contract.PHRASES; these sentences are used only at test time. Set A renames each concept (synonyms and clinical terms); set B describes it in plain words. concept/concept_id follow data_contract.PHASES and data_contract.TOOLS. How they were made: drafted by the authors with the help of an AI assistant, then checked against published definitions, listed in "sources" (the Cholec80 phases and its tool rule: a tool is present when at least half of its tip is visible; the phase descriptions of the TUM LapChole dataset, which uses the same phases plus a separate trocar-placement phase; standard anatomical and instrument terms). They were not reviewed by a clinician.
sources: Twinanda et al., EndoNet: A Deep Architecture for Recognition Tasks on Laparoscopic Videos, IEEE TMI 2017 (arXiv:1602.03012): the 7 Cholec80 phases and 7 tools; a tool is present if at least half of its tip is visible.

Stauder et al., The TUM LapChole dataset for the M2CAI 2016 workflow challenge, arXiv:1610.09278: what each phase contains (preparation begins after the last trocar is placed; clipping and cutting of the cystic duct and artery; the liver bed is cleaned and checked for bleeding; the gallbladder is packed in a plastic retrieval bag, which is pulled out of the body in the retraction phase).
Jones et al., Anatomy, Abdomen and Pelvis: Gallbladder, StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf NBK459288): the hepatocystic triangle, also termed the triangle of Calot; the gallbladder bed of the liver.

Kelly, Laparoscopic retrograde (fundus first) cholecystectomy, BMC Surgery 2009;9:19: the standard first step places a grasper on the gallbladder fundus and elevates the liver to expose Calot's triangle.

AORN, Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy (2023): the instruments (blunt grasping forceps, electrocautery hook, laparoscopic scissors, clip appliers, laparoscopic irrigator and suction, specimen retrieval bag); the gallbladder is dissected off the liver bed, placed in the retrieval bag and removed through a port.

B.description: plain descriptions: what happens in each phase, and what each instrument does or looks like (a tool counts as present when it is visible, as in the Cholec80 tool labels)
